parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi Charles, I'm writing my report on the songwriting course for drama students You know the one week residential course for drama students from different universities where you learn about writing songs Ydid that course last year didn't you? Could you give me some tips for the report? I'm having a few problems with it.

Yes, it was great. Well Lorna you could start by thinking about what you gut of it.

Evaluating how useful it was is simple but the challenge is not to goover length.

Referring to published sources might help. That would make it more scholarly too.

Okay, I'll go with that.

And saying why you did the songwriting course is important. Some people judo it as another string to their bow to help with aulitions for work and things. I thought it was a good opportunity to try out nw techniques for communicating feelings and emotions. I was already confident about singing before I did it.

I thought it was the location of the course which made it special being hea country house rather than in a university They were doing some building work on part of the house though so it wasn't always ey to concentrate.

I enjoyed the workshop most. How about you?

Well, we were divided into six small groups for the afternoon each with their own advisor That was the best bit for me, having that discussion with an expert. When we got into pairs to start wriings, the idea was to combine people with different levels of knowledge and experience. But my partner preferred working on her own generally.

And what did you think of the course content? I hadn't realised beforhow important the structure of a song is to its success.

Yes, we learned it's no use writing the most beautiful words and meleodies if there's no shape. And we learned about the importance of a chorus in a song.

I knew about that stuff from my singing classes. It's a bit obvious, isn't it?

No, I suppose so. It was the input on lyrical styles and forms that I fouand tedious. You could always look them up on the web.

Anyway, how did you get on with writing your song?

It was tough, and Peggy, my partner, was hard work, which wasn't funny Andwas a slow process as a result of our lack of communication. By the time we finished, I was exhausted.

Writing music from the heart is like that, especially by the end of a course.

Well, that's got the report sorted. Thanks. Have you decided which teacher's workshops you're going to do next term?

I want to do Bob Lacy's. He's got a brilliant reputation for vvoice coaching, you know, getting us to use dialects and different pronunciation and stuff. He gets you to do things like weed out a newspaper article in character. It's amazing.

I'm thinking of going to Evelyn Chance's workshop.

Oh, Evelyn. She's quite a character. Is she running the stage fights ceourse again?

Yes, fencing and pretend punches and throwing techniques. She really knows how to help actors use the whole of the space available.

Lots of people like Ted Winter's workshop.

He knows how to deliver. He's keen on actors conveying emotion through their bodies and faces alone. It's a great way to reveal complex relationships and situations to an audience without makiing a speech of any kind I'm definitely going to sign up for that one.

If you want to understand a director's ideas, Kevin Gray'sworkshop would be perfect for you. He likes telling people what to do and he's always saying you can't have a company of acteprs reading a play anyway they want because they'd end up fighting amongst themselves. They must listen to the director.

What about Dorothy Thomas? She's good at activities for geetting rid of stress and, you know, emptying your mind of all thoughts about the past. And that can really help when acting.

Well, I think I'll put my name down for...

questions.question: What problem is Lorna having with her report?

analyses.content: Lorna 说评估课程很简单，但挑战在于“不要超长（not to go over length）”，也就是要遵守字数限制。
Evaluating how useful it was is simple but the challenge is not to go over length.
你可能听到 “Evaluating” 就想选 C，但那是她觉得简单的部分，不是问题所在。

questions.question: Why did Charles take the song-writing course?

analyses.content: I thought it was a good opportunity to try out new techniques for communicating feelings and emotions. I was already confident about singing before I did it.
你可能听到 “job prospects” 或 “auditions” 就选 A，但那是“有些人（Some people）”的目的，不是 Charles 的。
Charles 认为这是一个尝试交流“感觉和情绪（feelings and emotions）”新技巧的好机会，这对应自我表达。

questions.question: Which type of work did Lorna most enjoy?

analyses.content: Well, we were divided into six small groups for the afternoon each with their own advisor. That was the best bit for me, having that discussion with an expert.
虽然提到了 pair work（结对），但 Lorna 说她的搭档更喜欢独自工作（working on her own），这让她很累，并不是她享受的部分。
Lorna 说她最喜欢的部分是下午被分成“六个小组（six small groups）”并有顾问指导。

questions.question: Which aspect of the course content did both students find interesting?

analyses.content: I hadn't realised before how important the structure of a song is to its success. Yes, we learned it's no use writing the most beautiful words and melodies if there's no shape.
Charles 觉得 Chorus（副歌）太明显了，觉得 Lyrical styles（歌词风格）很枯燥（tedious），所以这两个不是共同兴趣点。
Lorna 意识到歌曲的“结构（structure）”很重要，Charles 也同意如果没有“形状（shape）”写再好的词也没用。
It was tough, and Peggy, my partner, was hard work, which wasn't funny... By the time we finished, I was exhausted.
Lorna 说这个过程 "wasn't funny"（并不好玩），直接排除了 amusing（有趣的）。
Lorna 说因为缺乏沟通导致进度很慢，到完成时她感到“筋疲力尽（exhausted）”，对应累人。

analyses.content: Charles 说 Bob Lacey 擅长教大家使用“方言（dialects）”和不同的发音，对应各种口音。
He's got a brilliant reputation for voice coaching, you know, getting us to use dialects and different pronunciation and stuff.
不要听到 newspaper article 就想选 F，那是用来练习口音的道具，不是即兴表演。
Yes, fencing and pretend punches and throwing techniques. She really knows how to help actors use the whole of the space available.
虽然提到了 stage fights（舞台打斗），但这只是为了引出她对空间利用的教学重点，不要过度联想动作本身。
Charles 说 Evelyn 真的知道如何帮助演员利用“全部可用的空间（whole of the space）”，对应充分利用舞台。
He's keen on actors conveying emotion through their bodies and faces alone. It's a great way to reveal complex relationships and situations to an audience without making a speech of any kind.
听到 "without making a speech" 就要排除任何与语言相关的选项，直接锁定肢体表达。
Charles 说 Ted 喜欢演员仅通过“身体和脸（bodies and faces alone）”来传达情感，不做任何演讲。
He likes telling people what to do and he's always saying you can't have a company of actors reading a play anyway they want... They must listen to the director.
你可能听到 reading a play，但那是为了说明 Kevin 不允许演员随意发挥，必须听指令。
Charles 说 Kevin 喜欢“告诉人们该做什么（telling people what to do）”，演员必须听导演的。
She's good at activities for getting rid of stress and, you know, emptying your mind of all thoughts about the past.
你可能听到 "past" 就想选 A（回忆），但录音说的是 "emptying your mind of... past"（清空关于过去的思绪）。
Charles 说 Dorothy 擅长通过活动帮大家“消除压力（getting rid of stress）”和放空思绪。
